title: ai lets me spend my time on the ideas and the feel instead of building systems. here's how we make our telemarketing bullet-hell with a coding agent
author: WritingDecent9543
selftext:
ColdCall: Sales Champion is a dark comedy where you cold-call strangers to sell them wealth products, and every call is a dodge fight against what the customer says. the idea came from a chinese short story about doing telesales in guangzhou, and the dodge fights are inspired by undertale. almost all the code is written with a coding agent (claude code), and the art starts from gemini images. it's not one-shot vibe coding though, here's what's actually behind it:

1. **our own engine.** under the game there's a 2d engine on top of FNA that we share across all our games: interactive music, asset loading straight from aseprite files, quests, saves, dialogue, localization, particles, collision, an imgui debug layer and more. every part kept getting reworked while we built the games, and there's still the unglamorous stuff at the end like performance work.
2. **markdown docs are the real code now.** the agent reads a rules file every session (pixel rules, naming, how to verify things, which branch is for what). there are 26 design docs, plus a shared repo with standards (pixel art, pixel fonts, recordings) and 18 workflows like steam release, localization and music production. i still make the calls: every decision gets a date in the doc, so the agent doesn't quietly undo it.
3. **the agent can't see my screen, so it checks itself.** the game has headless modes: render any screen to a png, or let a bot play a whole in-game month on a hidden device. a lot of checks fail by themselves, like a portrait covering a UI line or a button a gamepad can't reach. bots at three skill levels also play the month in parallel for balance.
4. **rules are code, not comments.** dodge patterns are json, and each one gets a "human limit" check: lethal bullets need at least 0.6s of warning, no more than about 4 harmful emitters at once, gaps wider than the player's heart plus 6px. the agent can't make something unfair without seeing a warning.
5. **ai art, rebuilt.** gemini gives a source image, a tool rebuilds it onto a real pixel grid, and everything is locked to fixed palettes (16 colors for characters and UI, 11 for backgrounds). i review every file and mark it final; if it changes later it goes back to "needs review". the app icon i drew by hand lol
6. **translation in tiers.** 25 languages, translated by ai with a glossary and a sheet for how each character talks in each language. for the main 8, all 3,155 lines are sorted into 4 tiers: ai is fine / ai is shippable but a proofread helps / a human would clearly do better / chinese joke that needs rewriting. only the last two go to human translators, for brazilian portuguese that's about 126 lines, and we're starting with a paid test on just those.

and yeah, i've had people tell me my game feels very ai, which is honestly annoying. it's like i bought a motorbike to get around, and people tell me it's loud and bad for the environment. they have no idea how much time i spend maintaining it, cleaning it and polishing it. of course, using ai to copy someone else's work is shameful, i agree with that.

steam page if you want to see more: https://mingo.games/s/cc-7x6x

happy to answer anything about the setup.

comments.author: babaganoosh43
comments.body: Very cool, how long did it take you?

replies.author: WritingDecent9543
replies.body: thanks! not counting the engine and the basic systems, close to 2 months

comments.author: Human-Tangerine4573
comments.body:
There's maybe a cumulated thirty seconds of actual bullet hell type gameplay. The game looks alright but if someone told me "here's a bullet hell" I would feel a bit disappointed. 

Also, personal opinion: the "texts" on the right take up maybe a fifth of your screen and adds nothing, there's already progression, win/fail feedback in every screen. For something purely aesthetic (from what I can tell), it's way too big and the playing area way too small in comparison.

replies.author: WritingDecent9543
replies.body: thanks, that's fair. "bullet hell" is probably the wrong word, dodging is only one part of the loop. the text on the right is actually the phone conversation, the bullets are the customer's words coming out of it, but if that doesn't read at first glance that's on me. from what you saw, how would you describe the genre?

replies.author: Human-Tangerine4573
replies.body:
Well yeah, I know it's the customer words, it reads as such, my point is that (at a glance) it adds absolutely nothing to the actual gameplay experience and takes a fifth of your screen. That's bound to annoy some players on smaller screens and poses some accessibility issues when the playing area is smaller.

On the genre I can't really help you or tell you from a trailer, you should know roughly what your genre is before advertising it or you will lose your target audience (which is hard to have to begin with if you're not sure what you're selling).

replies.author: WritingDecent9543
replies.body: i'll think about it. we're going to next fest in february, so there's still time to change things. if more people complain about the right side, it definitely has to change

comments.author: Ashamed-Cost-5548
comments.body:
your motorcycle mtaphor does not makes sense. I mean I can agree that it is annoying. But how would the fact that you maintain it well change the fact that it is loud and the smog is making people cough. 

if anything maybe you could polish it until no one complains anymore.

or well embrace it but dont expect the complainer to lick you ass. simple

replies.author: WritingDecent9543
replies.body: fair, the metaphor isn't perfect lol. i'll just keep polishing
